ORAL JUDGMENT (PER: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VENKATESH NAIK T)
1.

These appeals are filed by the State Authorities challenging the common judgment and award dated 24.03.2017 passed in LAC Nos.13/2010, 14/2010 and 15/2010 by the learned Prl. Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Belagavi1, whereby the Reference Court enhanced the market value of the subject lands at Rs.45,000/- per gunta with all statutory benefits, costs and interest.
2.

The respondents/claimants are the owners of land bearing RS No.175/1B measuring 1 acre 2 guntas (LAC No.13/2010), RS No.176/1A & RS No.176/1B measuring 31 guntas(LAC No.14/2010)
and RS No.176/2 measuring 31 guntas respectively.
The said lands are situated at Hirebagewadi village, Belagavi Taluk & District.
The appellants/State under preliminary notification dated 17.05.2007 acquired the subject lands for the purpose of construction of Primary Health Centre and Quarters.

The appellant/SLAO passed an award dated 24.11.2009 'Reference Court', for short NC:
2024:KHC-D:18073-DB determining the market value of the acquired land at the rate of Rs.6,85,000/- per acre.
Being aggrieved by the same, the respondents/claimants sought reference before the Reference Court.
The reference Court under impugned judgment and award, enhanced the market value of the acquired land at Rs.45,000/- per gunta with all statutory benefits, costs and interest.
Aggrieved by the same, the State is before this Court in these appeals.

3. Learned AGA appearing for the appellants/State vehemently contends that the reference Court failed to consider that the acquired lands are agricultural lands and the SLAO has taken into consideration the prevailing market value by considering the surrounding developments and after verifying the sale statistics of the lands sold in the said village for the period of three years preceding the date of issuance of preliminary notification.

Secondly, the reference Court committed an error in holding that the acquired lands have got non-agricultural potentiality by placing reliance on judgment passed in the acquisition proceedings in respect of National Highway Authority, Dharwad (Ex.P19 in LAC NC: 2024:KHC-D:18073-DB No.13/2010) and after giving 10% escalation per year,
fixed the market value at Rs.45,000/- per gunta, which is arbitrary and without any basis.

Thirdly,
the reference Court without any basis and material on record wrongly came to a conclusion that the acquired lands are also situated adjacent to National Highway and the lands are having non- agricultural potentiality and therefore, fixed the market value of the acquired lands, which is unjust and unreasonable.

Lastly, the reference Court on the basis of assumption and presumption came to the conclusion that in the year 2007, the market value of the land acquired for National Highway Authority might be Rs.46,301.50 by adding 10% escalation to the award passed in the judgment pertaining to acquisition proceedings to the National Highway Authority, Dharwad.
Hence, the market value determined by the reference Court in respect of subject lands at the rate of Rs.45,000/- is erroneous and arbitrary.
Thus, he prays for allowing the appeals.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondents/claimants supports the impugned judgment and NC: 2024:KHC-D:18073-DB award of the reference Court.

He further submits that while passing the award, the reference Court has taken all relevant aspects as to the date of acquisition, market value, potentiality of the land, loss sustained to the owner of the land, location of the land and has rightly granted suitable compensation.
Thus, he prays for dismissal of the appeals.

5. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the material available on record including the original records, the following point would arise for our consideration in these appeals:
"Whether the Reference Court has justified in re-determining the market value of the acquired land at the rate of Rs.45,000/- per gunta with all statutory benefits, costs and interest"?
6.

The undisputed facts are that the respondents/claimants are the owners of land bearing RS No.175/1B measuring 1 acre 2 guntas (LAC No.13/2010), RS No.176/1A & RS No.176/1B measuring 31 guntas(LAC No.14/2010) and RS No.176/2 measuring 31 guntas respectively.
The said lands are situated at Hirebagewadi NC: 2024:KHC-D:18073-DB village, Belagavi Taluk & District.
The appellants/State under preliminary notification dated 17.05.2007 acquired the subject lands for the purpose of construction of Primary Health Centre and Quarters.
The appellant/SLAO passed an award dated 24.11.2009 determining the market value of the acquired land at the rate of Rs.6,85,000/- per acre.
Being aggrieved by the same, the respondents/claimants sought reference before the Reference Court.
The reference Court enhanced the market value of the acquired land at Rs.45,000/- per gunta with all statutory benefits, costs and interest.
7. In this case, the State sought for reduction of the compensation.

Admittedly, the subject lands are acquired in the year 2007 and 4(1) notification was issued on 17.05.2007 and SLAO passed an award on 24.11.2009 determining the market value of the acquired land at Rs.6,85,000/- per acre.
Therefore, the core issue would be, whether increase should be at a cumulative rate or flat rate.
The increase in the market value is calculated with reference to the market value during the immediate preceding year.
When the market value is sought to be ascertained with reference to a transaction which took place some years before the acquisition, the method adopted is to calculate the year to year increase.
As the percentage of increase is always with reference to the previous years' market value, the appropriate method is to calculate the increase cumulatively and not applying a flat rate.
In this case, the properties acquired is attached to the National Highway and the market value fixed for NA land was taken for consideration to fix the market value of the acquired land.
The market value of the property acquired by the NHAI, Dharwad was Rs.26,136/- per gunta in the year 2001, as can be seen in Exs.P19, P13 and P8 respectively.
Hence, 10% of the escalation per year has to be increased.

If 10% of the value is increased per year from the period 2002 to 2007,
then the total market value comes to Rs.45,000/- and it would be just and proper to award market value of the acquired land at Rs.45,000/- per gunta.

Thus, taking note of all these aspects into consideration, the reference Court has rightly fixed the market value of the subject lands at the rate The Assistant Commissioner vs Fakirappa Durgappa Talawar on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83938843/
5 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:18073-DB of Rs.45,000/- per gunta, which in our view is just and reasonable.
8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the preceding analysis to the aforesaid extent, the appellants have not made out any grounds to interfere with the impugned judgment and award of the reference Court.

Accordingly,
the appeals filed by the State are dismissed being devoid of merit.
The registry to transmit the TCR to the reference Court forthwith.
